description: Real-time anomaly detection engine that correlates time-series signals across distributed services and surfaces root causes before on-call pages fire
opening_quip: Superintendent Chalmers, I must report that Team Temporal has submitted something that, by the standards of this institution, qualifies as genuinely remarkable — a phrase I do not deploy lightly, having once awarded that distinction to a particularly well-formatted CSV file.

dimensions.name: Architecture
dimensions.subtitle: Code structure, layering, and separation of concerns
dimensions.evidence: cmd/, internal/detector/, internal/correlator/, internal/alerter/ with strict import boundaries enforced by go.work. Detector and correlator are interface-driven; three concrete implementations each. No import cycles; depguard enforces boundaries in CI.
dimensions.quip: The import graph is cleaner than Springfield Elementary's fire-safety plan, and I mean that as the highest compliment I am structurally capable of giving.

dimensions.name: Integrations
dimensions.subtitle: External systems wired together and called at runtime
dimensions.evidence: Prometheus scrape + remote-write ingestion, PagerDuty Events API v2, Slack webhooks, ClickHouse for series storage, Redis for sliding-window state, and OpenTelemetry trace export to Jaeger. All clients retry with exponential backoff; secrets via environment injected from Vault.
dimensions.quip: Six live integrations including two time-series stores and an alerting chain — I had to re-read the submission twice, and then I had to sit down.

dimensions.name: Problem Difficulty
dimensions.subtitle: Inherent hardness of the core problem attempted
dimensions.evidence: Streaming multivariate anomaly detection with ADWIN drift detection, causal graph correlation across 40+ signal types, and sub-500ms root-cause attribution. The sliding-window percentile estimator handles out-of-order arrivals without buffering unbounded state.
dimensions.quip: Causal correlation across forty signal types with bounded memory is the sort of problem that ends PhD dissertations, and they did it in a weekend, which I find personally unsettling.

dimensions.name: Scope Delivered
dimensions.subtitle: How much works end-to-end in the hackathon window
dimensions.evidence: Live demo ingesting 12k metrics/sec from a synthetic chaos harness, surfacing anomalies with contributing signals within 480ms median latency. Slack alerting, PagerDuty suppression, and a read-only Grafana dashboard all functional at submission.
dimensions.quip: A working demo at twelve-thousand metrics per second is not the work of people who padded their timeline — it is the work of people who, I suspect, did not sleep.

dimensions.name: Engineering Rigor
dimensions.subtitle: Test coverage, CI pipeline, error handling, code quality
dimensions.evidence: 91% line coverage across 74 test files including property tests via rapid (Go). CI runs staticcheck, golangci-lint, go vet, race detector, and integration tests against a real ClickHouse and Redis via Docker Compose. Benchmark suite with regression thresholds enforced in CI.
dimensions.quip: A race-detector-clean benchmark suite with property tests and 91% coverage is the kind of engineering rigour I describe to new students as a hypothetical, because I had assumed it did not exist in the real world.

dimensions.name: Innovation
dimensions.subtitle: Novelty and creativity of the approach or solution
dimensions.evidence: ADWIN-based drift detection applied to cross-service correlation windows rather than single streams; causal graph is built online using a streaming PC algorithm variant. The suppression model learns from historical page noise to avoid alert storms during known deployment windows.
dimensions.quip: An online causal discovery algorithm applied to alert suppression is the sort of idea that makes me wonder whether I have been grading the wrong things for the past eleven years.

dimensions.name: Operational Readiness
dimensions.subtitle: Containerization, deployment, observability, and reproducibility
dimensions.evidence: Multi-stage Go builder image, distroless runtime, non-root uid 65532. Helm chart with readiness/liveness probes, HPA based on queue depth. Grafana dashboard as code (grafana-operator CRD). OTEL trace sampling configurable at runtime. make demo spins the full stack in Docker Compose in under 90 seconds.
dimensions.quip: A distroless image, a Helm chart, and a one-command demo environment — I am beginning to suspect this team has done this before, which would technically violate the spirit of a hackathon, but I cannot prove it and so I will simply note it for the record.

closing_quip: Sixty-four out of seventy. Grade: A. This is the highest score I have awarded in four years of running this rubric, and I want it noted that I did not inflate it — I simply ran out of reasons not to give the points. Team Temporal has built something that would not embarrass a Series B infrastructure company, and they did it in forty-two hours. I am proud of them, and I resent that I feel that way.
